The 19.2.6-0ubuntu0.24.04.1 package in noble-proposed removes the `auth_supported` option, which breaks libvirt RBD storage pools on noble (confirmed regression). A respin that restores the option (.2, currently only in a PPA) must be uploaded and verified before release.

SRU team and the uploader asked to keep this in noble-proposed until the libvirt bug LP #2172324 is resolved. The block-proposed-noble tag is still set, and there is no coordination yet, such as a Breaks against older libvirt, to prevent regressions for users who upgrade only one of the two packages.

19.2.6 contains the CephX CVE fix and changed key handling. Releasing it before the 20.2.4 SRU reaches resolute and stonking would create an upgrade regression window, and SRU policy requires the fix to be in later series first. The 20.2.4 SRU is still pending.
The libvirt/arm64 autopkgtest regression triggered by ceph in noble-proposed was reported and has not been shown to be resolved. It may be related to the `auth_supported` removal.

The noble `verification-done-noble` tag was set before the `auth_supported` regression was found. The verification applies to the .1 build, so it must be redone on the respun .2 package, and the `verification-caracal-needed` tag is still outstanding.

The bug description's update list does not mention the compatibility patch that restores `auth_supported`. The Regression Potential section is a generic statement that does not address the libvirt/CloudStack breakage or the changed CephX behaviour. Both should be updated to reflect the respin.

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html
